clue.text: Priceless mineral found in mountain pass

indicators.note: the mineral is said to be found within the pass, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
mica is a flaky silicate mineral

explanation.surface: A rare and valuable mineral turns up in an Alpine pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' suggests great value, but here it means hilariously funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless in its colloquial sense means hugely amusing, which is what funny or comic things are.

clue.text: Offcut of rock appearing on the surface

definitions.text: Offcut of rock appearing on the surface

parts.words: Offcut of rock appearing on the surface
parts.note: read 'Offcut' as two words, off (out) and cut (crop), and the whole describes a piece of bedrock showing above ground

explanation.surface: A trimmed chip of stone has surfaced in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the term for bedrock that is exposed at the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Test side batting needs help in upset

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for help is read upwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A cricket team at the crease needs assistance after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AID into DIA. A Test is an international cricket match, so a Test side is a national team.
explanation.definitionFit: India fields a national cricket team that plays Test matches, so it is an example of a Test side.

clue.text: Stop when confronted by snake on the road

indicators.note: the word for stop has the snake placed in front of it, facing it

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls up on meeting a snake lying across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'on the road' is the definition, describing the surface material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry paving material laid on road surfaces, so it is what you find on the road.

clue.text: Hoped to rise from despair

indicators.note: the letters rise up out of the word and are reformed, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tried to climb out of hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise from' rearranges DESPAIR; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something, so aspired is a synonym of hoped.

clue.text: Bird captured by cunning, taking one's time

indicators.note: the bird is held inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A crafty trap catches a bird at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without hurrying, taking one's time, is doing it at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Put in a grave concept during TV discussion

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a view is an idea or opinion

explanation.surface: A grim burial idea is floated on a television chat show.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast question-and-answer session with a guest is a common form of television discussion.

clue.text: Capricious boy about to betray one's trust

indicators.note: the boy's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: A fickle lad is on the point of letting down a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to betray one's trust' reads as part of the surface story, but it is the verb rat, as in ratting on a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable and changeable, which is what capricious means.

clue.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

definitions.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

parts.words: They tend to bring up unrelated issues
parts.note: sounds like people who raise irrelevant points, but 'issues' means offspring: carers who raise children not their own

explanation.surface: Some people habitually raise irrelevant topics in discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adults who raise children not biologically theirs, temporarily or long term, are the carers described.

clue.text: The poker players' boss?

parts.note: a boss is an ornamental knob, and one kind of poker is named after such a knob

explanation.surface: Who is in charge of the card players?
explanation.walkthrough: Stud is a form of poker, and a stud is also a boss, a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a protruding knob or boss, and also the name of a variant of poker.

clue.text: Head ball on to rightwinger

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance or ball
taken as written
a Tory is a British Conservative, of the political right

explanation.surface: A footballer heads the ball on to the right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. In the surface 'Head' is a football action; it is the definition, a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A head in geography is a headland, a high point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Equip a girl for naval war service

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is kitted out to join the navy in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships assembled for war at sea.

clue.text: Permit, strange to relate

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: It is allowed, curiously, to tell the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the letters of TO RELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to allow or put up with it, so it is a synonym of permit.

clue.text: Gluttons may have one; Alexander the Great didn't

definitions.text: Gluttons may have one; Alexander the Great didn't

parts.words: Gluttons may have one; Alexander the Great didn't
parts.note: big eaters carry a roll of fat at the waist, while Alexander besieged and destroyed the Phoenician city of Tyre rather than sparing it

explanation.surface: Something overeaters own but a famous conqueror lacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is a roll of belly fat. Alexander sacked Tyre in 332 BC: he did not spare it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang names a roll of fat around the waist after an extra wheel, and the phrase also reads as a mercy not shown to a city.

clue.text: Two blues for British hearties

parts.note: royal blue is a shade of blue
navy blue is a shade of blue

explanation.surface: Two shades of blue stand for British sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearties is an old word for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearties are sailors, and the British fleet's sailors make up the nation's sea service.

clue.text: Desert watercourse

definitions.meaning: a narrow channel dug to carry water

explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to abandon, and a ditch is a narrow channel for drainage water.

clue.text: Navy man and journalist

definitions.meaning: the diarist was a senior administrator of the English Navy Board
here in its old sense of someone who keeps a journal or diary

explanation.surface: A sailor who also writes for the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys ran naval administration under Charles II and kept a famous daily journal.

clue.text: Eastern politician, queen or ruler

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's monogram
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Asian statesman may be a queen or a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Guard what one says — a good maxim

parts.note: to watch is to guard
a word is something said

explanation.surface: Be careful what you say: that is sound advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a motto or guiding principle, much like a maxim.

clue.text: Saucy way to join those in the lead?

definitions.text: Saucy way to join those in the lead?

parts.words: Saucy way to join those in the lead?
parts.note: the spelling of a tomato sauce doubles as a phrase meaning to draw level with the leaders

explanation.surface: A cheeky method of reaching the front runners.
explanation.walkthrough: Catchup is a variant spelling of ketchup, the sauce; to catch up is to reach those ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw level with those ahead is to close the gap, and the same letters spell a tomato sauce.

clue.text: Adam disturbed, bolted out fast

indicators.note: the word for bolted is placed outside the rearranged name

parts.note: ran means bolted, fled

indicators.note: the name's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Adam was upset and dashed off at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles the name to AMAD. 'fast' is the noun, a period of going without food, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month during which Muslims abstain from food in daylight.

clue.text: Speak quietly, but possibly from the heart

definitions.meaning: to talk in a low soft voice
an abnormal sound a doctor may hear in the heart

explanation.surface: Talk softly, but perhaps sincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: To murmur is to speak softly, and a heart murmur is an unusual cardiac sound.

clue.text: Acclaim new papal practice

indicators.note: the word papal is made new, rearranged

parts.note: use means custom or practice

explanation.surface: A fresh custom from the Vatican is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is public approval shown by clapping, a form of acclaim.

clue.text: Shock of university graduate after painting is rejected

indicators.note: the university and graduate pieces come after the reversed painting
rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: painting is art
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate is stunned when their painting is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is severe emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: Old car doesn't start, causing exasperation

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, worn-out car

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car that won't start makes its owner furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is British slang for an old car; 'doesn't start' drops its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperation is intense irritation, a form of anger.

clue.text: Game for an experimental marriage?

definitions.meaning: a sporting fixture played to assess players
a match is a marriage, and a trial is a test run

explanation.surface: A game for a couple trying out wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial match tests players for selection, and read literally it is a test union.

clue.text: Gallery idols

definitions.meaning: the highest, cheapest seats in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: The top gallery of a theatre is called the gods, and gods are idols worshipped.

clue.text: Mixed up Presbyterians not best in these?

definitions.text: Mixed up Presbyterians not best in these?

indicators.note: the letters of the churchgoers are jumbled, and some removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Muddled churchgoers may not be at their finest in worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the letters of BEST and IN from an anagram of PRESBYTERIANS, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitions offered to God are what Presbyterians say in church, so the whole clue points at them.

clue.text: Frank on horseback at the battle zone

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
the front is where fighting takes place

explanation.surface: A man named Frank rides into battle at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the definition, meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upfront is being open and honest, which is what frank means.
